hd_auger2016 (Auger 2016, NRF 146)

Differences with CFSForestTools

CFSForestTools generalhdrelation2014 (commit fa86f80c, LGPL-3, https://github.com/CWFC-CCFB/CFSForestTools) agrees with the published NRF 146 model for only 10 of 27 species. Comparison against its unit-test file fichier_test_unitaire_smaller.csv (200 trees per species; all PERT = NON, SDOM 1/2est/2ouest):

Agreement Species (QC codes) max |Δh| (m)
Matches (within rounding) CET, ERA, FRA, FRN, MEL, ORA, OSV, PIB, PIR, TIL ≤ 0.016
Close EPB 0.062
Differs CHR 2.57, BOG 1.73, BOJ 1.24, PEG 1.18, HEG 1.06, EPR 0.99, PEB 0.85, ERS 0.47, BOP 0.39, PIG 0.30, THO 0.25, PRU 0.22, PET 0.20, SAB 0.19, EPN 0.16, ERR 0.14 —

Observed causes. The per-species parametersXXX.csv files appear to come from a different fit than the one published: - BOG: CFSForestTools includes TMOY and VP; the publication has BA only and no ln(DBH+1)² term. - BOJ: CFSForestTools adds SDOM and MP. - EPB: CFSForestTools has no FC1 VP level and adds an ldhp × pert term. - CFSForestTools parameters have full precision. The published values are rounded to 4 decimals, so the ALT and PTOT slopes carry about one significant digit (up to about ±0.15 m effect).

The package follows the publication. CFSForestTools is used as a benchmark only for the 10 matching species: tests/testthat/test-hd_auger2016.R and tmp/generate_hd_auger2016_comparison_values.R. Full analysis: data-raw/Auger2016_model-spec.md (benchmark section).

Actions

    • Is the CFSForestTools parameter set a later or revised fit of the NRF 146 model? Is it documented anywhere (reference, date)?
    • Which version is recommended for the 17 differing species?
    • Can full-precision versions of the published (NRF 146) coefficients be obtained, especially the ALT and PTOT slopes?
    • Is the missing EPB FC1 level, and the extra ldhp × pert term, intentional?

hd_eslamdoust2026 (Eslamdoust et al. 2026, FST 22:217–230)

Details: data-raw/Eslamdoust2026_model-spec.md (⚠1–⚠4, benchmark plan).

    • Tamarack M5 α2: printed 0.9793. The package uses 0.09793, an inferred correction. Fig. 3b fits it with RMSE 0.93 m. A free fit to the figure gives about 0.126, but the same method misses basswood’s α2 by 13%. Which value is correct?
    • Table 2 AIC for yellow birch (M4 7977 > M5 7969) contradicts the text (p. 222), which says M4 is better.
    • TPH threshold: “DBH ≥ 2.5 cm” (p. 220) vs “DBH > 2.5 cm” (p. 222).
    • BA (BAH) minimum DBH, and whether SHT and BAH are all-species or species-specific. Neither is stated.
    • The Fig. 3a hemlock curve is drawn 0.4–0.6 m below the Table 4 M4 prediction along its whole length (all other species within 0.5 m). Was it drawn from a different fit?

hd_sharmaparton2007 (Sharma & Parton 2007, FEM 249:187–198)

Details: data-raw/SharmaParton2007_model-spec.md (review decisions, ⚠ flags, Stage 2 outcome).

    • BA (BA/ha) minimum DBH. Not stated; only N/ha is defined (DBH ≥ 2.5 cm, p. 188).
    • Stand origin: tree origin (natural/planted) was recorded (p. 188), but were planted trees excluded? The registry uses stand_origin = "both" as an assumption.
    • Table 6 typos, which do not affect predictions: jack pine M2 σ²_u SE printed (0.00001), which is implausibly small; balsam fir M2 γ SE is missing a parenthesis.

hd_huang2016 (Huang, Yang & Aitkin 2016, Alberta T/609)

Details: data-raw/Huang2016_model-spec.md (review decisions, ⚠ flags, implementation notes).

    • Table 18 (SAS IML program) is the reference implementation.
    • Table 12 column 5 (fixed-only SW predictions) can serve as a benchmark; the first rows are already reproduced in the spec.

hd_auger2025 (Auger, DeBlois & Lambert 2025, SSS-10)

Details: data-raw/Auger2025_model-spec.md (review decisions, benchmark plan).

    • Below the dominant DBH, "dominant" agrees with hd_auger2016, hd_huang2016 and hd_sharmaparton2007 within about 2 m.
    • Above it, "dominant" flattens toward the dominant height and runs 2–7 m lower at DBH 25 cm.
    • Likely a genuine plantation effect; mention it in the HD vignette.
    • See tmp/generate_hd_auger2025_comparison_values.R.

General

    • hd_auger2016 uses French source acronyms (TMOY, PTOT).
    • hd_auger2025 uses English names (mean_DBH, dominant_DBH).
    • Decide on one convention. Renaming arguments is an API change: deprecate the old names rather than removing them.
